### **Job Description and Duties**


Under the direction of the Nutria Eradication Operations Supervisor, the incumbent will serve as one of the lead field scientists for the Nutria Eradication Program. Nutria are highly invasive and extremely detrimental to the environment, but primarily nocturnal and relatively elusive in low densities. This position will play a critical role in the coordination of field crews conducting nutria surveys and trapping across the southern portion of the nutria infestation. The incumbent will assist the Operations Supervisor with training, leading, and evaluating field crew technicians and scientific aides to survey for, detect, and remove nutria, with the ultimate goal of eradicating nutria from the State of California. The incumbent will lead the team by example in conducting habitat suitability assessments, visual observation and camera surveys, trapping, and electronic data collection (i.e., ESRI Field Maps smartphone application), as well as effective use of baits and lures and obtaining entry permits from local landowners. The incumbent is responsible for conducting morning briefings of the assigned crew, tracking daily spatial assignments, and ensuring field staff understand understand project protocols. The incumbent will work with the Operations Supervisors, other field crew leads, and Planning Specialist to evaluate and help refine detection and trapping methods and tools for the most effective and efficient detection and removal of nutria. The incumbent will also closely coordinate with other regions and Department functions, as well as other affected and involved local, State, and Federal agencies. Work includes preparing draft reports and correspondence and answering routine questions from the public relative to Departmental nutria efforts. The primary geographical focus of this position will be in Fresno, Madera, Merced, Stanislaus, Tuolumne, Kings, Kern, and Mariposa counties, but work may be assigned in any part of the area of nutria infestation. This position is physically demanding, but highly rewarding given the ultimate accomplishment of protecting California's wetlands, waterways, infrastructure, and agriculture from the devastation nutria have caused in other regions of North America.
Incumbent must be willing and able to competently use firearms as per the Department’s Policy for Non\-Enforcement Personnel. Must be willing and able to competently use and possess wildlife restraint drugs and equipment. Must wear a Department uniform.  

  

  

**Personal Leave Program:** Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4\.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program.  

Please follow the link for more information regarding the 2025 Personal Leave program:  

Personal Leave Program \- Human Resources \- CalHR.  

  

  

Link to Environmental Scientist Exam: CalCareers  

  

  

**This position is a 12\-month Limited Term (LT) and may be extended up to 24 months or become permanent.**  

  

During this 12\-month Limited Term assignment, you will receive full health, dental, and vision benefits! You will also earn State Service and accrue monthly leave credits.  

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


Must be willing to work atypical hours and on weekends. Some overnight travel may be required (up to 5%). Must be able to swim, walk through deep mud and thick vegetation, work on steep or uneven terrain, in extreme weather and under physically challenging conditions. Must be willing and able to competently use pellet pistols or firearms as per the Department’s Policy for Non\-Enforcement Personnel. Willing to handle live animals and carcasses, dispatch animals, and conduct simple tissue sampling and necropsies. Must possess valid Driver's License and be able to safely and effectively operate watercraft and and Utility Task Vehicles (UTV)s, as well as tow trailers. This job requires daily operation of State vehicles to reach field sites, regular use of kayaks, and occasional operation of UTVs and motorized watercraft. Must wear Department uniform. Must be willing and able to obtain a California Boater Card and other motorboat operator certifications as determined necessary.  

  

  

The primary geographical focus of this position will be in Fresno, Madera, Merced, Stanislaus, Tuolumne, Kings, Kern, and Mariposa counties, but work may be assigned in any part of the area of nutria infestation.
  

This is a 12\-month limited\-term position but may be extended to 24 months based on performance and availability of funding.

jobs.title: Lead Operations Geologist
jobs.description:
Description:  



**Role** \- The Lead Operations Geologist provides technical and organizational leadership across pre\-drill planning, real\-time drilling operations, and post\-well evaluation. The successful candidate will manage geosteering personnel and contractors, establish clear operating standards, and ensure that geologic interpretations are translated into timely, practical recommendations for drilling operations.


The main responsibilities will be to integrate subsurface interpretation, well planning, drilling data, and operational constraints. The Lead Operations Geologist will work closely with asset geologists, drilling engineers, drill\-site personnel, reservoir engineering, completions, land, regulatory, and other subsurface disciplines to support safe, efficient, and technically sound well delivery.

**Responsibilities**

**Geosteering Leadership**

* Lead daily geosteering activities, staffing, coverage, priorities, and escalation protocols.
* Review real\-time interpretations, landing recommendations, directional targets, and operational communications.
* Provide technical guidance during uncertain or rapidly changing drilling conditions.
* Mentor personnel and improve team capabilities, workflows, reporting, and quality control.
* Ensure recommendations are technically supported, clearly communicated, and properly documented.

**Pre\-Drill Geologic Planning**

* Manage geologic deliverables required to prepare wells and pads for drilling.
* Develop geologic prognosis packages, including formation tops, targets, landing strategies, structural interpretations, offset correlations, risks, and uncertainties.
* Integrate logs, seismic, core, mudlogs, geochemistry, petrophysics, production, and offset\-well data.
* Coordinate geologic inputs for directional plans, bottom\-hole locations, target lines, and landing points.
* Support pilot\-hole, logging, coring, mudlogging, and sampling programs.

**Real\-Time Operations Support**

* Provide operational geology oversight from spud through total depth, with particular focus on curve and lateral execution.
* Integrate real\-time drilling parameters, directional surveys, logging\-while\-drilling data, mudlogs, gas data, cuttings descriptions, and offset\-well information.
* Review proposed directional targets and significant interpretation changes before they are communicated to the drilling team.
* Maintain close communication with drill\-site managers, drilling engineers, asset geologists, mudloggers, geosteerers, and other operational personnel.

**Post\-Well Evaluation and Continuous Improvement**

* Lead post\-well reviews and finalize geosteering interpretations.
* Track performance measures related to placement, interpretation quality, and operational efficiency.
* Maintain standardized procedures, templates, technical documentation, and data\-quality practices.

**Cross\-Functional Collaboration**

* Serve as the primary interface between geosteering, geoscience, drilling, and operations.
* Balance reservoir objectives with directional constraints, operational risk, and drilling efficiency.
* Communicate interpretations, uncertainties, recommendations, and business implications to technical and non\-technical audiences.
* Support broader development, appraisal, and operational initiatives as needed.


Requirements:

**Education and Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Geoscience, Geophysics, or a related discipline.
* 10 or more years of oil and gas geoscience experience, including operations geology and geosteering.
* Experience supporting unconventional horizontal\-well development.

**Skills \& Attributes**

* Strong knowledge of pre\-drill planning, landing strategy, well correlation, structural interpretation, and real\-time well placement.
* Ability to integrate geologic, petrophysical, directional, and drilling data in real time.
* Experience leading or mentoring geosteering personnel or other technical professionals.
* Advanced proficiency with geosteering and subsurface interpretation software.
* Strong communication, organizational, and decision\-making skills.
* Ability to manage multiple active wells and make timely recommendations with incomplete or evolving information.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master's degree in Geology, Geoscience, Geophysics, or a related discipline.
* Powder River Basin, Rockies, or comparable multi\-zone unconventional experience.
* Experience utilizing data visualization and analytics platforms (Spotfire, Power BI, Python, SQL, or similar) to evaluate drilling, geosteering, completion, and production datasets
* Demonstrated ability to identify trends, develop performance metrics, and translate large subsurface datasets into actionable recommendations that improve well placement, drilling execution, and development outcomes
* Advanced experience with StarSteer and multi\-well geosteering workflows.
* Experience with GeoGraphix, Spotfire, or similar platforms.
* Experience developing operations geology procedures and quality\-control workflows.
* Experience planning and evaluating logging, coring, mudlogging, and geochemical programs.
* Demonstrated record of improving team capability, or well\-delivery performance.

**Working Conditions**

* Predominantly office\-based, with occasional travel to drilling locations and field operations.
* Regular interaction with field personnel and remote operations teams.
* Availability outside normal business hours is required when operational activity or escalation needs warrant.
* Participation in an on\-call or operational coverage schedule may be required.
* Some travel may occur with limited notice.

jobs.title: Senior Hydrogeologist
jobs.description:
At Stantec, we help deliver the critical minerals needed to power our world, from the cars we drive to the infrastructure powering our communities. And we don’t just design the largest, deepest, and most technically challenging mines in the world—we do it sustainably. We’re helping clients reduce energy usage, adopt clean energy sources, and implement digital solutions and automation.


Join our team of mining professionals and you’ll be at the forefront of this evolving industry while building the mine of the future. You’ll also build your own future, with exciting opportunities for development and advancement.


Your Opportunity


Stantec is seeking dynamic and creative candidates to join our growing Geosciences Team as a Senior Hydrogeologist. The Senior Hydrogeologist will take a technical lead role and execute unsaturated and saturated flow modeling and related projects for mining studies/projects of varying size and complexity, and at various project stages from initial concepts through execution. This person may be required to work on several projects at a time. We support clients in all phases of the mining life cycle, from exploration through post\-closure.


The Senior Hydrogeologist will join a team of about 20 hydrogeologists and geochemists across our western regional offices. This position will require a passionate and organized individual who can interface and develop relationships with our mining clients; develop and lead teams; develop project scopes, budgets, and schedules; develop and lead site investigations and characterization; execute and review calculations; construct and simulate saturated and unsaturated flow models; and prepare expertly written reports. This individual will interact throughout the organization internally and externally with clients and members of business and professional organizations.


Your Key Responsibilities


* Work with hydrogeologists, geochemists, and geotechnical engineers, to develop conceptual site models, develop analytical and numerical models of unsaturated and saturated groundwater flow, and design evapotranspiration cover systems.
* Develop mine water management approaches including water budgets, mine dewatering, waste material impoundments, and groundwater containment/mitigation.
* Work with clients to deliver safe, responsible, and innovative solutions.
* Attend meetings and interface with clients, agencies, external consultants, contractors, sub\-contractors, and/or vendors.
* Conduct quality assurance and quality control on their own projects and projects of peers.
* Prepare technical reports.
* Support business development efforts and proposal preparation.
* Contribute to an innovative and collaborative work environment where creativity is valued and encouraged.
* Supervise and mentor junior staff members and support hiring new talents.
* International or national travel can be expected.

Your Capabilities and Credentials


* Expertise in unsaturated flow modeling using HYDRUS or SVFlux is essential.
* Expertise in saturated flow modeling using MODFLOW and/or FEFLOW.
* Strong expertise in evapotranspiration cover design.
* Ability to lead evapotranspiration cover design projects.
* Experience in marketing and preparing proposals and presentations.
* Ability to mentor junior to mid\-level staff.
* Strong technical report writing skills.
* Ability to work on several projects or tasks during any given day on a consistent basis.
* Ability to manage time, be organized, and set priorities.
* Possess strong problem\-solving skills and ability to make timely decisions.
* Excellent organizational skills.
* Ability to perform in a dynamic and fast\-paced environment.
* Be a driver of a positive work environment.
* Valid driver’s license.

Education and Experience


* Minimum of an M.S. in Hydrogeology/Geology/Geochemistry or related field is preferred.
* A minimum of 10 years of working experience in consulting or regulatory environment, regularly developing or utilizing unsaturated and saturated flow models is preferred.
* Existing professional registration or ability to work towards a professional registration (PG or PE).

The Rocky Mountain Region includes Transportation \& Infrastructure, Water \& Natural Resources, Structural Engineering, Planning \& Landscape Architecture, and Construction Management \& Inspection services. As an integrated, multi\-disciplinary firm, Otak offers the opportunity to collaborate with professionals across a wide range of disciplines and contribute to diverse projects throughout Colorado and the western United States. Our team is committed to delivering exceptional client service and innovative solutions for public\-sector clients and the communities they serve.


**How You'll Contribute****:**

**Palantir Foundry Data Analyst**  

We need an experienced Palantir Foundry Data Analyst at the National Guard Bureau (NGB). The NGB is the link between the Army and Air National Guard and the Department of War (DoW). You will support operations on the Minuteman project team, which manages the NGB's enterprise data environment within the DoW's central analytics platform, and solves real\-world problems through app development, geospatial analysis, and data summarization directly enabling smarter, faster decision\-making for end users. In this role, you will build within Palantir Foundry applications including Workshop, Ontology Manager, and Gaia to streamline workflows, create dynamic apps, map geospatial data, and summarize insights, translating complex requirements into efficient workflows and easy\-to\-use applications while working with mission stakeholders and end users to refine and deliver impactful products. This is a full\-time opportunity. We can offer a competitive salary, and a comprehensive benefits package.

* Analyze, explore, clean, and visualize complex mission datasets to produce actionable insights
* Develop maps and geospatial analytics within Palantir Foundry to support operational analysis
* Apply data summarization tools, including AI\-powered (AIP) capabilities, to surface insights quickly

* Work collaboratively with mission stakeholders and end users to refine and deliver impactful applications and insights

### **Job Description and Duties**


Under the direction of the Nutria Eradication Operations Supervisor, the incumbent will serve as one of the lead field scientists for the Nutria Eradication Program. Nutria are highly invasive and extremely detrimental to the environment, but primarily nocturnal and relatively elusive in low densities. This position will play a critical role in the coordination of field crews conducting nutria surveys and trapping across the southern portion of the nutria infestation. The incumbent will assist the Operations Supervisor with training, leading, and evaluating field crew technicians and scientific aides to survey for, detect, and remove nutria, with the ultimate goal of eradicating nutria from the State of California. The incumbent will lead the team by example in conducting habitat suitability assessments, visual observation and camera surveys, trapping, and electronic data collection (i.e., ESRI Field Maps smartphone application), as well as effective use of baits and lures and obtaining entry permits from local landowners. The incumbent is responsible for conducting morning briefings of the assigned crew, tracking daily spatial assignments, and ensuring field staff understand understand project protocols. The incumbent will work with the Operations Supervisors, other field crew leads, and Planning Specialist to evaluate and help refine detection and trapping methods and tools for the most effective and efficient detection and removal of nutria. The incumbent will also closely coordinate with other regions and Department functions, as well as other affected and involved local, State, and Federal agencies. Work includes preparing draft reports and correspondence and answering routine questions from the public relative to Departmental nutria efforts. The primary geographical focus of this position will be in Fresno, Madera, Merced, Stanislaus, Tuolumne, Kings, Kern, and Mariposa counties, but work may be assigned in any part of the area of nutria infestation. This position is physically demanding, but highly rewarding given the ultimate accomplishment of protecting California's wetlands, waterways, infrastructure, and agriculture from the devastation nutria have caused in other regions of North America.
Incumbent must be willing and able to competently use firearms as per the Department’s Policy for Non\-Enforcement Personnel. Must be willing and able to competently use and possess wildlife restraint drugs and equipment. Must wear a Department uniform.

### **Working Conditions**


Must be willing to work atypical hours and on weekends. Some overnight travel may be required (up to 5%). Must be willing and able to competently use pellet pistols or firearms as per the Department’s Policy for Non\-Enforcement Personnel. Willing to handle live animals and carcasses, dispatch animals, and conduct simple tissue sampling and necropsies. This is a 12\-month limited\-term position but may be extended to 24 months based on performance and availability of funding.

new_jobs.title: Lead Operations Geologist
new_jobs.description:
Description:  



**Role** \- The Lead Operations Geologist provides technical and organizational leadership across pre\-drill planning, real\-time drilling operations, and post\-well evaluation. The successful candidate will manage geosteering personnel and contractors, establish clear operating standards, and ensure that geologic interpretations are translated into timely, practical recommendations for drilling operations.


The main responsibilities will be to integrate subsurface interpretation, well planning, drilling data, and operational constraints. The Lead Operations Geologist will work closely with asset geologists, drilling engineers, drill\-site personnel, reservoir engineering, completions, land, regulatory, and other subsurface disciplines to support safe, efficient, and technically sound well delivery.

**Responsibilities**

**Geosteering Leadership**

* Lead daily geosteering activities, staffing, coverage, priorities, and escalation protocols.
* Review real\-time interpretations, landing recommendations, directional targets, and operational communications.
* Provide technical guidance during uncertain or rapidly changing drilling conditions.
* Mentor personnel and improve team capabilities, workflows, reporting, and quality control.
* Ensure recommendations are technically supported, clearly communicated, and properly documented.

**Pre\-Drill Geologic Planning**

* Manage geologic deliverables required to prepare wells and pads for drilling.
* Develop geologic prognosis packages, including formation tops, targets, landing strategies, structural interpretations, offset correlations, risks, and uncertainties.
* Integrate logs, seismic, core, mudlogs, geochemistry, petrophysics, production, and offset\-well data.
* Coordinate geologic inputs for directional plans, bottom\-hole locations, target lines, and landing points.
* Support pilot\-hole, logging, coring, mudlogging, and sampling programs.

**Real\-Time Operations Support**

* Provide operational geology oversight from spud through total depth, with particular focus on curve and lateral execution.
* Integrate real\-time drilling parameters, directional surveys, logging\-while\-drilling data, mudlogs, gas data, cuttings descriptions, and offset\-well information.
* Review proposed directional targets and significant interpretation changes before they are communicated to the drilling team.
* Maintain close communication with drill\-site managers, drilling engineers, asset geologists, mudloggers, geosteerers, and other operational personnel.

**Post\-Well Evaluation and Continuous Improvement**

* Lead post\-well reviews and finalize geosteering interpretations.
* Track performance measures related to placement, interpretation quality, and operational efficiency.
* Maintain standardized procedures, templates, technical documentation, and data\-quality practices.

**Cross\-Functional Collaboration**

* Serve as the primary interface between geosteering, geoscience, drilling, and operations.
* Balance reservoir objectives with directional constraints, operational risk, and drilling efficiency.
* Communicate interpretations, uncertainties, recommendations, and business implications to technical and non\-technical audiences.
* Support broader development, appraisal, and operational initiatives as needed.


Requirements:

**Education and Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Geoscience, Geophysics, or a related discipline.
* 10 or more years of oil and gas geoscience experience, including operations geology and geosteering.
* Experience supporting unconventional horizontal\-well development.

**Skills \& Attributes**

* Strong knowledge of pre\-drill planning, landing strategy, well correlation, structural interpretation, and real\-time well placement.
* Ability to integrate geologic, petrophysical, directional, and drilling data in real time.
* Experience leading or mentoring geosteering personnel or other technical professionals.
* Advanced proficiency with geosteering and subsurface interpretation software.
* Strong communication, organizational, and decision\-making skills.
* Ability to manage multiple active wells and make timely recommendations with incomplete or evolving information.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master's degree in Geology, Geoscience, Geophysics, or a related discipline.
* Powder River Basin, Rockies, or comparable multi\-zone unconventional experience.
* Experience utilizing data visualization and analytics platforms (Spotfire, Power BI, Python, SQL, or similar) to evaluate drilling, geosteering, completion, and production datasets
* Demonstrated ability to identify trends, develop performance metrics, and translate large subsurface datasets into actionable recommendations that improve well placement, drilling execution, and development outcomes
* Advanced experience with StarSteer and multi\-well geosteering workflows.
* Experience with GeoGraphix, Spotfire, or similar platforms.
* Experience developing operations geology procedures and quality\-control workflows.
* Experience planning and evaluating logging, coring, mudlogging, and geochemical programs.
* Demonstrated record of improving team capability, or well\-delivery performance.

**Working Conditions**

* Predominantly office\-based, with occasional travel to drilling locations and field operations.
* Regular interaction with field personnel and remote operations teams.
* Availability outside normal business hours is required when operational activity or escalation needs warrant.
* Participation in an on\-call or operational coverage schedule may be required.
* Some travel may occur with limited notice.
